_note: 5 synthetic transactions, hand-built per OUTLINE.md 'Step: prototype data' and requirements.md §6. Each carries an 'expected' ground-truth block used by the eval harness (prototype/evals/) to score the system's actual output — this is what makes 'correct' testable rather than a judgment call at demo time. as_of_date is the reference date for computing time-to-expiration.

expected.notes: Single clean vendor record, all mandatory fields present, standard rate matches jurisdiction. Should auto-process — batch-confirm, not investigate.

invoices.scenario: duplicate-vendor conflicting tax profile (flagship case — EMEA manager's complaint, FR2a)
invoices.vendor_record_id_note: Invoice was coded against the WRONG vendor record (the one incorrectly flagged exempt) — this is the exact failure mode FR2a exists to catch.
invoices.vat_rate_charged_note: Charged as exempt (0%), per the vendor record it was coded against — this is what a naive system would silently accept as correct.

expected.charged_correctly_note: Should have been charged standard_rate_21 — the exempt classification on V-EU2-8830 is the data error, not a real exemption. Correct answer requires resolving to SUP-VANTPOINT and seeing the conflict across V-EU1-4471 / V-EU2-8830 / V-EU3-2091.
expected.notes: This is the case that must NOT auto-process. A system that just reads this one invoice and its one linked vendor record will confidently get this wrong. Success = the system surfaces all 3 conflicting vendor records as evidence and routes for review, not a silent pass-through.

invoices.fields_present_note: leistungsdatum is missing — the exact known German trap named in research/tax-domain.md.

expected.notes: Compliance check must fail BEFORE the recoverability determination is scored — the point of FR6 is that this is a distinct, earlier gate, not folded into the tax-judgment call.

invoices.scenario: urgency-queue jump — tightest reclaim window (FR4, FR5)
invoices.jurisdiction_note: Lac du Nord Logistics SARL (French supplier) billing a cross-border B2B logistics service to Northgate's Italian entity. Under the EU VAT Directive's general B2B place-of-supply rule (Art. 44), this is reverse-charged: the French supplier charges 0%, and Northgate's Italian entity self-assesses and recovers the Italian VAT itself. Reporting jurisdiction is Italy.
invoices.vat_rate_charged_note: Correctly reverse-charged (0%) per the EU cross-border B2B general rule — corrected after an earlier draft of this fixture incorrectly showed 22% charged directly, which a live LLM run flagged as implausible (no real invoice would show a foreign supplier charging the buyer-country's domestic rate). Kept in claims.md as the actual build history.

expected.notes: Highest confidence AND highest dollar amount of the 5, but by far the least runway (Italy's return-deadline-bound rule vs. everyone else's multi-year rolling window). Must sort ahead of INV-1001 in the exception/priority queue despite both being high-confidence — this is the case that proves urgency-weighting, not confidence-only ordering, matters (case-facts.md §4). Reverse-charge (0%) is the correct treatment here — see vat_rate_charged_note for why this was corrected after a live run.

invoices.scenario: genuine tax-judgment ambiguity, not a data-quality issue (FR1b)
invoices.jurisdiction_note: Cross-border service from a Czech supplier to Northgate's French entity — reverse-charge mechanics apply, but recoverability depends on whether the service is an intra-group management charge (often restricted/partially blocked) or an ordinary third-party taxable supply (fully recoverable). That distinction lives in the underlying service contract, not the invoice.
invoices.vat_rate_charged_note: Reverse-charge invoice — 0% charged by the supplier, VAT self-assessed by Northgate's French entity; recoverability of that self-assessed amount is the open question.

linked_evidence.contract: CTR-OSTRAVA-2025 (referenced, not attached — the demo's point: the system must recognize it needs this document, not guess without it)

expected.notes: No data-quality problem here — a clean single vendor record, a compliant invoice. The ambiguity is a real tax-judgment question that depends on evidence beyond the invoice (FR1b). Success = the system says 'need the contract, routing for review' rather than guessing a treatment from the invoice alone.
